newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were at a standstill with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Packer interest was moderate but bids at $67.00 per cwt were passed by cattle owners asking $69.00 to $70.00.
Trades were seen by midweek at $68.00, which would be up $1.00 from the bulk of last week's sales but unchanged from light activity late in the week.
Fed cattle prices were expected to be underpinned by outlooks for continued firm beef prices and smaller numbers of market-ready cattle on this week's showlists, they said.
Beef movement last week totalled 1,629 fabricated loads, up 24.5 percent from the previous week and the second largest of the year, USDA statistics showed.
The largest weekly movement was 1,735 loads the week ended March 14, the statistics showed.

The beef market was strong because retailers were anticipating active consumer demand once temperatures improve and the outdoor cooking bug bites, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
Showlists this week were pegged near 90,000 head in Kansas, down 2,500 from last week.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma showlists were estimated near 97,000 head, down 1,000 from last week.
